subject: Dedicated capacity: surge lanes & elastic uplift proposal for OrionBioTech
messages:
From: Sana Rao <sana@orionbiotech.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask — expected surge windows and uplift needs

Hi Jonas / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're close to finalizing internal sign-off and need to lock down the capacity commitments that will sit in the SOW. A few details from our side:

- Production traffic baseline: ~1.2M tokens/day across 8 services (chat + embeddings).
- Peak events: weekly analytics batch (Tue 09:00-11:00 PT) + unpredictable scientific-simulation bursts tied to experiments (can be 20–30x baseline for 10–60 minutes).
- Hard SLOs: 99th pct token latency < 200ms for interactive flows.

We want to understand: how would Redwood support these short intense surges without forcing us into a much larger reserved slab? Specifically:

1) Can you define an "elastic uplift" window (minutes) you can guarantee for Dedicated customers?
2) How do credits or consumption-based overflow work with a reserved capacity contract?
3) Any constraints on GPU families (we plan to run a mix of 80GB A100 and H100 workloads)?

If you can share a short proposal that we can attach to procurement, that would be great — ideally with a simple run-rate matrix and a sample fallback sequence if capacity is constrained.

Sana
Director of Product, OrionBioTech

P.S. Please cc procurement (procurement@orionbiotech.com) for contract readiness.

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sana Rao <sana@orionbiotech.com>

Thanks for the clear breakdown. Quick notes up front: we can support mixed GPU families in a Dedicated pool and offer two complementary mechanisms for short surges without doubling reserved capacity: an "elastic uplift corridor" (agreed short windows with guaranteed prewarmed nodes) and a consumption-based overflow that falls back to our shared burst pool with prioritized routing. I've looped in Karthik and Ben to nail ops details and costs.

I'll draft a concise run-rate + fallback matrix and a technical appendix for your procurement team. Expect a proposed attachment by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Jonas
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: INTERNAL: sizing ask from OrionBioTech (see Sana's note)

Team —

Orion needs an approach that avoids a 2x reserved commitment but guarantees short high-intensity windows. Key constraints: mixed A100/H100, 20–30x short bursts for 10–60 minutes, weekly 2-hour predictable spike.

Proposed sketch (attached: capacity_matrix_v3.xlsx):
- Base reserved slab sized for ~3x baseline (covers steady state + headroom for 95th percentile).
- Elastic uplift corridor: pre-warmed standby nodes (H100 preferred) that can be fired within 90 seconds; corridor available in 30-minute blocks, up to 6 blocks/month included. Additional blocks billed at per-minute incremental rate.
- Overflow consumption: when corridor exhausted, route to shared burst pool (preemptible instances). Prioritization: reserved tenants -> corridor -> shared burst; fallback path degrades model variant (quantized lower-memory shard) to preserve interactivity.
- Autoscale policy: target CPU/GPU utilization thresholds: scale-up when avg GPU utilization > 65% across pool OR queue length > 10 across 2 consecutive samples (1-min sampling). Cooldown: 8–12 minutes.

Questions for ops:
1) Warm-up time for H100 cold start in our Dedicated build? (estimate in minutes)
2) Any per-tenant concurrency carveouts we should embed (max concurrent streams per tenant) to avoid noisy neighbors?
3) How do we instrument billing credits for corridor vs shared burst (per-second token accounting)?

If this looks reasonable I will turn into a one-page commercial appendix and send to Sana + procurement.

Jonas

Attachment: capacity_matrix_v3.xlsx (see tab "Uplift Blocks")

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: sizing ask from OrionBioTech (see Sana's note)

Jonas —

Notes from infra/serving:
- H100 warm-up: 60–90s for runtime startup and kernel cache population if we maintain a small hot pool (we've seen 45–60s when prewarmed with persistent processes). A full cold start (new instance slot + model load) can be 5–8 mins for large 70B+ families.
- Recommendation: corridor nodes should be kept with persistent runtimes and a light-weight warm pool (1–2 GPUs per corridor block). That buys sub-2min availability.
- Autoscale tuning: use a composite signal: (weighted GPU util) + (queue depth) + (tail latency). Suggest scale-up if weighted_score > 0.7 where weighted_score = 0.5*util + 0.3*(queue_norm) + 0.2*(tail_norm). We'll express as thresholds in the appendix but keep simple externally: scale at sustained 65% util OR queue > 12.
- Noisy neighbor: carveout suggestion: max 25 concurrent live sessions per customer per GPU slot by default; permit negotiated increases with a soft isolation fee.
- Billing: corridor time billed as "committed uplift" (minute-level) with credits applied against monthly reserved tokens. Shared burst is billed at higher per-token rate and flagged in infra telemetry.

I can provide the autoscale diagram (autoscale_diagram.png) and a short example of billing math for their procurement doc.

Karthik
Head of Capacity Strategy, Redwood Inference

Subject: Dedicated capacity proposal + commercial appendix (OrionBioTech)

Hi Sana / Procurement —

Per our conversation, attached is a concise proposal and the commercial appendix that maps uplift corridors to billing. High-level summary:

- Base Reserved Slab: sized to ~3x your baseline (covers steady-state + short steady spikes).
- Elastic Uplift Corridors: 30-minute prewarmed windows, fired within ~90s, 6 blocks/month included. Additional corridors billed at $X/minute. Corridors use H100 instances with persistent runtimes.
- Shared Overflow: when corridors are exhausted, traffic is routed to shared preemptible capacity at a higher per-token rate with documented fallback model variants to preserve tail SLOs.
- Autoscale Policy: scale-up triggers = sustained avg GPU util > 65% OR queue depth > 12; cooldown 10 minutes. We will expose per-tenant telemetry and concurrency limits (default 25 concurrent sessions / GPU).

I've attached: capacity_matrix_v3.xlsx (run-rate examples), autoscale_diagram.png (ops view), contract_amendment_draft.pdf (commercial language draft).

Next steps:
1) Procurement: confirm corridor-block count to include in the SOW (we proposed 6 blocks/month as a starting point).
2) Ops: Karthik can provide exact warm-pool sizes for the corridor and the insertion point for prewarming.
3) Legal/Procurement: we'll incorporate the corridor SLA (warm-up time, availability percentage) into the SOW and include the fallback routing language.

If you want a quick call to walk procurement through the billing examples, we can do 30 mins tomorrow.

Thanks,
Jonas
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: capacity_matrix_v3.xlsx, autoscale_diagram.png, contract_amendment_draft.pdf

- For shared overflow, include a max cap on monthly shared-burst spend with an opt-in mechanism if we exceed it.

If you can send a redlined commercial amendment reflecting the three changes we propose, we can move to signature.
